clue.text: Boarding establishments?

parts.note: reads like lodging houses for paying guests, but the boarding here is planks of timber, so these are places where boards are produced

explanation.definitionFit: A mill that saws logs turns out boards, so it is literally an establishment making boarding.

clue.text: Wreck on a chart firmly fixed

indicators.note: to wreck something is to break it up, so the letters of the words that follow are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shipwreck is marked on a nautical chart, firmly fixed in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wreck' looks like a noun for a sunken ship on a chart; it is the anagram signal working on ON A CHART.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship moored by its anchor is held in place, so it is securely fixed.

clue.text: It's strictly true, but unimaginative

explanation.surface: Something is strictly accurate yet dull and lacking in imagination.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain fact is something strictly true, and a prosaic, unimaginative person or style is described with the same hyphenated phrase.

clue.text: Cupboard key

explanation.definitionFit: A cupboard with a lock, as in a school changing room, and also anything that locks, as a key fastens a door.

clue.text: Dad's embarked for health resorts

annotationWithheld.why: Dad's embarked for health resorts: PA'S inside SS, where 'embarked' both supplies SS (steamship) and signals the container, one word doing two jobs

clue.text: The loss in fuel is gigantic

indicators.note: the word loss is placed inside the word for the fuel, as the clue says

parts.note: coal is a fuel burnt in fires and furnaces
taken as written

explanation.surface: The amount of energy lost through wasted fuel is enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of vast size, like a huge statue.

clue.text: Mount hotly tipped when it runs

definitions.text: Mount hotly tipped when it runs

parts.words: Mount hotly tipped when it runs
parts.note: reads like a racehorse fancied by tipsters, but the mount is a Sicilian volcano that pours out hot lava when it erupts

explanation.surface: A horse strongly fancied by tipsters whenever it races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount' and 'hotly tipped' and 'runs' all suggest a racehorse; the mount is a mountain, a volcano whose lava runs hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known active volcano in Europe, in Sicily, whose eruptions send molten rock flowing.

clue.text: Old training manual

parts.note: suggests a dated handbook for instruction, but training means travelling by train and the manual is a timetable

explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian railway timetable guide named after its publisher George Bradshaw, the standard book for planning rail journeys.

clue.text: He puts a word in when required

definitions.text: He puts a word in when required

parts.words: He puts a word in when required
parts.note: sounds like someone who speaks up on another's behalf, but this is the person in the theatre wings feeding forgotten lines to actors

explanation.surface: Someone who offers a word of support whenever needed.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre the person following the script whispers a line to an actor who has dried.

clue.text: Lure one into a club

indicators.note: the letter for one goes into the word for the club, as the clue says

parts.note: a bat is a club used to hit a ball in cricket or baseball
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Tempt somebody to come and join a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Bait is food on a hook or in a trap used to tempt prey, just as a lure is.

clue.text: Receives an order and assumes control

parts.note: to take something is to receive it
a command is an order given to someone

explanation.surface: Someone gets an instruction and then takes charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking charge of a situation or a group of people is the same as assuming control.

clue.text: Be deadly serious about usury

explanation.surface: Someone is in earnest about the practice of lending money at high interest.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in earnest is an idiom with this phrase, and moneylending at extortionate rates is a stingy, miserly trade.

clue.text: Cathedral plans include religious education

indicators.note: the plans take the abbreviation for religious education inside them

parts.note: charts are maps or plans
RE is the school-subject abbreviation for religious education

explanation.surface: Drawings for a cathedral contain an element of religious teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: The cathedral is the great Gothic one in the French town southwest of Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: A French city famous for its Gothic cathedral and stained glass, the city's name standing for the building.

clue.text: Some music for a three-piece combination?

explanation.surface: Music written for a trio of players.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of instrumental pieces played in sequence, and a matching sofa and two armchairs sold together.

clue.text: Quickly take a few notes, maybe

explanation.surface: Jotting down a few notes in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To grab something suddenly, and a brief fragment of a song or tune heard in passing.

clue.text: It takes mostly hard work to make a tennis champion

indicators.note: only most of the word is wanted, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: graft is British slang for hard work

explanation.surface: Becoming a tennis champion demands a great deal of hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: Steffi Graf was a German tennis player who won many Grand Slam titles; GRAFT is British for hard toil.
explanation.definitionFit: Steffi Graf, German winner of twenty-two Grand Slam singles titles, is a famous champion of the sport.

clue.text: He's not alone in breaking the law

definitions.text: He's not alone in breaking the law

parts.words: He's not alone in breaking the law
parts.note: describes an accomplice, but the criminal is not alone because he belongs to a gang

explanation.surface: A criminal who has accomplices in his law-breaking.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of an organised criminal band, so always one of a group of crooks.

clue.text: Hearing noisy neighbour could be one

explanation.surface: Listening to a loud neighbour next door.
explanation.definitionFit: A case heard in court, and a burden or nuisance that tests one's patience.

clue.text: Worship money

explanation.definitionFit: To cherish or adore someone dearly, and a hoard of gold, jewels or wealth.

clue.text: Hear athlete is puffed

indicators.note: tells the solver to listen, so the word for the athlete is taken by its sound

parts.note: a Blue is a sportsperson who has represented Oxford or Cambridge University

explanation.surface: Listen to a sportsman who is out of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: A Blue is someone awarded colours for representing Oxford or Cambridge at sport, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffed and the past tense of breathe out forcefully are both ways of saying air was expelled.

clue.text: A time when the populace is at cross purposes?

definitions.text: A time when the populace is at cross purposes?

parts.words: A time when the populace is at cross purposes?
parts.note: suggests national disagreement, but people are making crosses on ballot papers to vote

explanation.surface: A period when the whole nation is at odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Voters mark a cross beside their chosen candidate during a polling contest to choose representatives.

clue.text: Write down some music? Not a note!

parts.note: taken as written
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone writes music down, yet not one note is set down.
explanation.definitionFit: To set music in written symbols on a stave is what it means to write it down.

clue.text: Did some relief work?

parts.note: suggests helping in a disaster, but relief means a raised design, as on metal or leather

explanation.definitionFit: Raising a design so it stands proud of a surface is crafting in relief.

clue.text: Game between two sides?

parts.note: sounds like any team match, but it is a card game and also a span linking two riverbanks

explanation.surface: A match between two competing teams.
explanation.definitionFit: A card game for four players in pairs, and a structure spanning two banks of a river.

clue.text: He figures a great deal in population surveys

definitions.text: He figures a great deal in population surveys

parts.words: He figures a great deal in population surveys
parts.note: suggests a prominent person in a census, but he works out numbers, figuring meaning calculating

explanation.surface: A man who features prominently in census reports.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert in numerical data who calculates averages and trends from survey results.

clue.text: Opening commercial with sex appeal

parts.note: an ad is a commercial advertisement
it is an old slang word for sex appeal

explanation.surface: An advert launched with plenty of sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: A horizontal entrance into a mine is an opening in the hillside.

clue.text: Lazy and backward in fielding

indicators.note: the run of letters found is read in reverse order
the letters are found inside the word fielding

explanation.surface: A cricketer who is lazy and slow in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' picks ELDI from inside 'fielding' and 'backward' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Being inactive and unwilling to work is the same as being indolent.

clue.text: The girl I get in the end

indicators.note: the letter I is placed inside the word for the end

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Finally, after all, I win the girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as of the children's author Blyton.

clue.text: Back number

parts.note: looks like an old issue of a magazine, but number means something that numbs, here the lower back

explanation.definitionFit: An anaesthetic injected near the spine numbs the lower body, often in childbirth.

clue.text: Not an odd tune for a church service

parts.note: a number that is not odd is even
a song is a tune

explanation.surface: A hymn sung in church that is not strange at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglican service of evening prayer, usually sung.
